claim: §3.4 *A layer's several arenas* (l. 3906–3908) says 'a raised way's two feet (`RaisedWayRecord.feet`, §2.7), where its ramps or stairs meet part 0 (item 110 (b))'. That restates where the feet lie, which is §2.7's to state, and contradicts §2.7 *At the frame*: a deck that ends on the outer ring has no ramp (VKr1-02).
required_change: §3.4: replace 'a raised way's two feet (`RaisedWayRecord.feet`, §2.7), where its ramps or stairs meet part 0 (item 110 (b)), each a `raised_foot` vertex on part 0 and one on the raised part' with 'a raised way's two feet (`RaisedWayRecord.feet`, §2.7; item 110 (b)), each a `raised_foot` vertex on part 0 and one on the raised part'.

claim: §3.3's KernelTx.expect (l. 3457) takes '§5.3's batch-scope invariants … the issuing stage's StageDecl.invariants of scope batch', and *Expectations* (l. 3488–3494) then rejects, repairs or downgrades on any failed entry. Round 1's §5.3 Invariant (l. 8823–8830) gives every row class 'hard'|'soft' ('hard: aborts the batch; soft (a statistics band): goes to the report'; likewise l. 8889–8890), and §3.1's E_INVARIANT (l. 3311) speaks of a hard invariant. A soft batch-scope entry, which the type admits, therefore has two outcomes: a rejected batch (§3.3) or a report line (§5.3).
required_change: §3.3 KernelTx.expect comment: '… the issuing stage's StageDecl.invariants of scope 'batch' and class 'hard' (§4.12, §5.3; a soft row goes to the report, never into `expect`), the class floors of the faces it makes among them (§4.7's class-floor row); …'.
